assertions.name: predictions_for_m_n_and_delta_pn_add_no_framework_content
assertions.source: Indicator (1 = both Delta_pn == Q_beta + m_e and m_n == m_p + Q_beta + m_e hold on the PREDICTION side to the dashboard's serialization granularity). Residuals are ~1e-11 MeV. This is the load-bearing claim: the framework has two independent quantities on the fail list, not five.

assertions.name: targets_are_no_longer_redundant_after_the_codata_fix
assertions.source: Indicator (1 = the TARGET side is no longer an exact identity). Pre-fix it was, because the neutron target was constructed from the proton and Q_beta. Repointing it at the independent CODATA direct determination is a gain in information content — asserted so a regression back to the constructed target would fail here rather than pass silently.

description: Separates prediction-side from target-side redundancy on the L2 dashboard. The PREDICTIONS for m_n and Delta_pn are exactly Q_beta/m_p plus m_e, so the framework has only two independent quantities on the fail list (Q_beta, m_mu) once m_p is recognised as an unscored anchor round-trip. The TARGETS stopped being redundant on 2026-08-09 when the CODATA vintage fix repointed the neutron at the independent direct determination — a gain in the dashboard's information content that does not add a third lever. Audit-only.

data.caveat: Prediction-redundant does not mean wrong to publish — m_n in MeV is a useful number. It means the row is not an independent test OF THE FRAMEWORK, so L2 planning must not count it as a separate front.
data.target_side_change_2026_08_09: Pre-fix the neutron target was M_N_MEV_AME_DERIVED, constructed as M_P + M_E + Q_BETA, so the target side was redundant too and the m_n row tested nothing new. It now points at M_N_MEV_CODATA_DIRECT, so ~0.16 ppb of independent experimental information enters.
